title: Club Membership: how the total reactivation payment amount is finalized
content:
## Scope
This document states, for Club Membership, how the current dues balance and the reactivation fee, after any employer-linked reduction, combine into the total amount the member must pay to reactivate the contract.

## Rule
The total amount collected is the current dues balance plus the reactivation fee reduced by the employer-linked combined percentage where one applies, rounded to 2 decimal places only at the end of the calculation, with no intermediate rounding. The total amount collected is never less than the current dues balance alone.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
Suppose the current dues balance is $60.00, the tier's own reactivation fee is $25.00, and an employer-linked combined percentage of 10 percent applies to the reactivation fee. The reactivation fee reduces to $22.50, and the total amount collected is $60.00 plus $22.50, giving $82.50.

## Points of judgement
Where the employer-linked combined percentage reduces the reactivation fee all the way to $0.00, the total amount collected is exactly the current dues balance alone, which is the floor this basis never goes below; the current dues balance itself is never reduced by any employer-linked percentage under this basis.
